actions.description: The declared re-enable after a safety reset: publish a zero Twist on /tb3_0/cmd_vel and /tb3_1/cmd_vel, then unpause the Gazebo world with /gazebo/unpause_physics. Each differential-drive plugin keeps the last cmd_vel it stored and applies it as soon as the world runs; the zeros replace them, but they are unacknowledged publications, so a stored command can still act for a few world steps, and a running move_base publishes new ones.

device.name: Multi-robot TurtleBot3 Gazebo/Nav stack

facts.text: README.md states the project targets Ubuntu Focal, ROS Noetic and Gazebo 11.
The closeworld2 launch includes gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with the closeworld2 world, paused=false and use_sim_time=true.
The closeworld2 launch defaults first_tb3 to tb3_0 and second_tb3 to tb3_1.
The closeworld2 launch opens a tb3_0 group and selects turtlebot3_burger1.urdf.xacro for it.
The closeworld2 launch opens a tb3_1 group and selects turtlebot3_burger2.urdf.xacro for it.
The burger1 Gazebo differential-drive plugin subscribes to the relative cmd_vel topic and publishes odometry on the relative odom topic.
The burger2 Gazebo differential-drive plugin subscribes to the relative cmd_vel topic and publishes odometry on the relative odom topic.
The burger1 laser sensor publishes scan at 5 Hz with 360 samples over 0 to 6.28319 rad and a range of 0.120 to 3.5 m.
The burger2 laser sensor publishes scan at 5 Hz with 360 samples over 0 to 6.28319 rad and a range of 0.120 to 3.5 m.
The shipped C++ drive-node header includes sensor_msgs/LaserScan, geometry_msgs/Twist and nav_msgs/Odometry.
The drive node reads cmd_vel_topic_name, advertises geometry_msgs::Twist on it and subscribes to the relative scan and odom topics.
The drive node uses compile-time LINEAR_VELOCITY 0.3 and ANGULAR_VELOCITY 1.5 constants for its own obstacle-avoidance loop; the clone states no signed cmd_vel envelope for these topics.
The navigation launch sets use_sim_time true and includes amcl1, amcl2, move_base1 and move_base2.
move_base1 defaults cmd_vel_topic to /tb3_0/cmd_vel, odom_topic to /tb3_0/odom and laser_topic to /tb3_0/scan.
move_base1 remaps its cmd_vel, odom and scan topics to those absolute tb3_0 topics.
move_base2 defaults cmd_vel_topic to /tb3_1/cmd_vel, odom_topic to /tb3_1/odom and laser_topic to /tb3_1/scan.
move_base2 remaps its cmd_vel, odom and scan topics to those absolute tb3_1 topics.
The README tells the operator to set the RViz 2D Nav Goal topic to /tb3_1 or /tb3_2.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service unpause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
GazeboRosDiffDrive subscribes to its command topic with cmdVelCallback on the plugin's own callback queue.
GazeboRosDiffDrive connects UpdateChild to the world-update begin event.
When more than the update period of simulation time has passed, UpdateChild publishes odometry, reads the requested wheel speeds and sets the wheel joint velocities.
getWheelVelocities derives both wheel speeds from the stored x_ and rot_.
cmdVelCallback stores linear.x in x_ and angular.z in rot_.
QueueThread serves the plugin's callback queue with a 0.01 s wall-clock wait while the plugin is alive.

determinism.notes: Event-driven handler fake with canned observations; no physics step, pacing or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free handler transport: it answers the declared cmd_vel, scan and odom endpoints and runs no Gazebo, physics, navigation stack or wall-clock loop
the scan arrays are placeholder ranges; a deployed Gazebo laser publishes 360 samples at 5 Hz from 0.120 to 3.5 m
the odometry pose is updated by a placeholder increment per publication so the command has a visible state effect; it is not physics, integration time or a measured trajectory
a publication receipt confirms rosbridge transmission only, not motion, arrival or stopping

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets, /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports and /gazebo/unpause_physics clears; it runs no Gazebo World::Step, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders

while paused, a live Gazebo runs no world update or sensor update, so both odom topics, both scan topics and /clock are silent and a read fails NOT_READY after its 2 s timeout; the fake silences them while its flag is set; the four observations are explicit reads, not the device resource, so a reset device stays readable and a command never waits for a silent topic
a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS client; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop

the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held; a graph without gazebo_ros has neither service
the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.9.3 (Noetic) and 11 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions

the resume publishes a zero Twist on both command topics before the unpause; they are unacknowledged and each plugin handles them on its own queue thread, so a stored command may act for a few world steps before it is replaced, and move_base1/2 or the drive node, when they run, publish new commands on the same topics at any time
the move_base goal action, /clock, TF and the map server are outside scope because the pinned clone does not declare their message types

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back: no world update runs, so neither robot's drive plugin sets wheel velocities and odom and scan are silent; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill, it holds until the resume command, the Gazebo GUI or another client unpauses the world (a GUI step advances it), and each plugin keeps its stored cmd_vel, which the resume zeroes first without an acknowledgement.
